# Phase 2 — Critique of Phase 1 and Twenty Improvements

The Awtsmoos renews the critic with the plan; what looked complete becomes a narrower span.
Awtsmoos.com deserves evidence stronger than enthusiasm can.

## Twenty Improvements To The First Plan

1. Separate route discovery from route execution so a bad page cannot prevent the inventory from completing.
2. Record route provenance: filesystem entrypoint, discovered link, test fixture, or dynamic route generator.
3. Create explicit allowlists for external/extension console noise so only site-owned errors fail the audit.
4. Capture response `Content-Type` for every module request, not merely status codes.
5. Treat 200-with-wrong-MIME as a first-class failure because `/apps` already demonstrates that class.
6. Detect HTML/JSON fallback bodies returned for missing static assets by inspecting both headers and leading payload shape.
7. Add case-sensitivity validation against actual filenames to prevent macOS-only success.
8. Detect imports that omit extensions only where the server/runtime requires explicit extensions.
9. Make route smoke tests wait for a stable quiet window after initial load rather than sampling too early.
10. Add per-page timeout budgets so one hung application does not stall the entire audit.
11. Audit authenticated and unauthenticated states separately where fixtures or safe session state exist.
12. Build API consumer mapping before changing any response contract, including fetch wrappers and direct `fetch()` calls.
13. Preserve endpoint aliases during API reorganization unless every consumer is proven migrated.
14. Add structured client-side error objects that retain HTTP status, endpoint, method, content type, and safe body excerpt.
15. Split CSS findings into global-foundation issues versus page-local issues; never solve local defects with wider global selectors.
16. Add viewport matrix receipts for mobile portrait, mobile landscape, tablet, desktop, and cinema-wide widths on representative interactive routes.
17. Include reduced-motion and keyboard-only verification in UI acceptance criteria.
18. Inspect deployment workflows before creating new scripts, so the canonical production path is strengthened rather than duplicated.
19. Create a pre-push secret/artifact review because the user explicitly requested committing unrelated changes too.
20. Require live post-deploy verification against the actual canonical URL and commit SHA before completion.

## Why The First Pass Was Not Enough

The first pass was expansive but could still confuse breadth with proof. It needed stronger provenance, MIME-level evidence, dynamic-route discipline, state separation, and a deployment/secret gate. The second pass turns broad intent into observable contracts.

## Revised Risk Graph

- Static routing -> MIME correctness -> module execution -> page boot.
- Page boot -> API transport -> endpoint contract -> UI state.
- UI state -> CSS scope -> responsive layout -> accessibility and cinematic presentation.
- Source rewrite -> tests -> build -> Git review -> push -> deployment -> live verification.
- Unrelated changes -> provenance -> secret/artifact review -> safe inclusion in commit.

## NEXT_ACTION

Write the improved brainstorm and executable file plan using these twenty upgrades, then run Git/runtime discovery.
